purpose: Require immutable competitor identities, matched semantics, and reproducible builds before comparative benchmarks are promoted.

competitors.name: RisGraph
competitors.comparison_scope: Exact directed incremental BFS under the official sliding-window batch semantics: add the next edge batch, remove an equally sized oldest batch, and maintain BFS from the same root.

competitors.name: Teseo
competitors.comparison_scope: Correctness-gated same-algorithm storage swap using BasicIncrementalBFS recomputation and mixed insertion/deletion batches; not a comparison with Teseo native algorithms or a system-level performance claim.

competitors.name: Sortledton
competitors.comparison_scope: Correctness-gated same-algorithm storage portability using BasicIncrementalBFS recomputation and deterministic mixed insertion/deletion batches; hosted timings are diagnostic only.

competitors.name: NetworkX
competitors.comparison_scope: Static/full recomputation reference only unless an exact matched dynamic workload is defined.

competitors.name: python-igraph
competitors.comparison_scope: Static/full recomputation reference only unless an exact matched dynamic workload is defined.

competitors.name: NetworKit
competitors.comparison_scope: Native NetworKit::DynBFS versus VeloGraphX exact directed dynamic BFS on identical streams, batches and three fixed roots per dataset, with full-BFS verification after every batch.

competitors.name: rustworkx
competitors.comparison_scope: Static/full recomputation reference only unless an exact matched dynamic workload is defined.

competitors.name: SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS/LAGraph
competitors.comparison_scope: Correctness-gated hosted BFS/SSSP engineering comparison using pinned GraphBLAS/LAGraph builds; dedicated-hardware publication execution remains outstanding.

competitors.name: GAP Benchmark Suite
competitors.comparison_scope: Correctness-gated hosted BFS/SSSP engineering comparison using GAP verification; official canonical GAP datasets and dedicated-hardware publication execution remain separate gates.

rules: Do not use floating labels such as latest, main, master or HEAD as publication pins.
Python competitors must record an exact package version and resolved distribution metadata.
Native competitors must record an immutable commit SHA or release tag plus compiler/build options.
A competitor may be marked ready only after its immutable identity, license, build recipe, and matched comparison scope are recorded.
Do not compare storage-only operations with incremental algorithm maintenance as if they were the same semantic operation.
Do not remove deletions, validation, or other difficult workload features merely because they disadvantage VeloGraphX.
Hosted CI results are engineering evidence and must not be described as universal or publication-grade performance claims.
notes: Ready means the immutable identity, build recipe and stated comparison contract are executable; it does not imply publication-grade evidence. RisGraph and NetworKit are accepted same-semantics dynamic-BFS baselines. Teseo and Sortledton are ready only for explicitly labelled same-algorithm storage portability/correctness experiments. GAP and LAGraph have successful hosted engineering campaigns, while dedicated-hardware publication execution remains outstanding.
